source: A hostile cross-origin but same-site sibling submits a simple POST with the victim's SameSite=Lax portal cookie to the fixed private:me read route.
control: Cookie authentication, tenant/thread authorization and a five-second repeat throttle hold, but the route omits assertAllowedTenantOrigin even though that exact-origin control is used by neighboring mutations.
sink: markCurrentUserThreadRead resolves the victim's conversation and invokes Chatwoot updatePublicConversationLastSeen/update_last_seen.
impact: The attacker can cause an unauthorized victim read/last-seen state mutation, creating a false read receipt and interfering with unread-state expectations; no data read, message send or tenant crossing is shown.
preconditions: Victim has a valid customer session and private conversation, visits an attacker-controlled same-site sibling origin, and the browser attaches the Lax cookie to the simple POST.

evidence.result: Exact source/control/sink trace is present and identical on both immutable baselines.
The authenticated mark-read route succeeds with 204 without an Origin header; the targeted suite passed.
The five-second throttle and thread authorization constrain frequency and object scope but do not validate request origin.

source: The claimed source requires possession of a still-fresh valid raw body, timestamp and HMAC while controlling only x-chatwoot-delivery; no lower-privileged repository path supplies that signed material.
control: HMAC over timestamp and raw body, five-minute tolerance, tenant payload invariants, TLS ingress and the backend-held tenant webhook secret hold; the delivery header itself is not HMAC-covered.
sink: Changing the delivery header selects a new tenant delivery key, so the same signed body can pass the delivery insert and repeat realtime/push side effects.
impact: The mechanical replay/dedupe bypass is demonstrated, but no realistic lower-privileged attacker gains it; a party with the signing secret can already sign arbitrary fresh events, and accidental upstream duplicates are reliability behavior.
preconditions: Attacker must observe a valid signed webhook within five minutes or already control the signing authority, then replay the identical body with a novel delivery header.

evidence.result: One identical body/signature was accepted and published twice when only the delivery header changed.
The signature excludes x-chatwoot-delivery and covers timestamp plus raw body only.
Targeted repository search found the secret/signature only in backend integration paths and tests, with no browser disclosure or lower-privileged signed-request source.

source: A tenant administrator retains a valid portal-admin cookie after Chatwoot demotes, disables or otherwise revokes that actor's administrator eligibility.
control: Session lookup checks tenant, token hash and expiry and returns the persisted administrator snapshot; the live Chatwoot eligibility service is not called by current-session resolution or the admin guard.
sink: The stale session passes requireTenantAdminSession and reaches protected tenant branding, legal-document and Telegram integration read/write operations.
impact: A revoked administrator retains same-tenant privileged authority for the remaining portal session lifetime, up to twelve hours absent logout.
preconditions: The actor was eligible when the portal session was issued, retains its signed cookie, is later revoked upstream, and uses a protected route before expiry or explicit logout.

evidence.result: Current account, confirmation, email and administrator role checks exist only in the separate live eligibility service.
The persisted session guard authorizes tenant branding mutations without a current Chatwoot decision.
The exposure is tenant-bound and capped by a fixed twelve-hour session lifetime.
The existing finding rechecks eligibility only before session creation and therefore does not remediate later active-session revocation.

source: Authenticated customers create successful tenant/user/thread read and typing throttle keys over process lifetime; missing or failed typing-off leaves typing keys behind.
control: Authorization, repeat-key overwrite and short throttle windows hold, but neither map has TTL/size eviction and read keys have no deletion path; typing deletion requires a successful matching off.
sink: Application-lifetime Map instances retain keys and separate replicas enforce independent throttle state.
impact: SaaS-wide key cardinality can grow for process lifetime and horizontal replicas can bypass each local read/typing window, increasing memory and upstream work.
preconditions: Many authorized tenant/user/thread tuples accumulate over time or traffic alternates across multiple backend replicas; strongest cardinality growth requires sustained tenant/thread churn.

evidence.result: The non-evicting read store and conditionally evicted typing store are identical across baselines.
Targeted tests confirm shared process-local repeat throttling and delete-on-off behavior; the suite passed.
The existing finding names both retained-key and cross-replica paths and its TTL/size/shared-routing remediation fully subsumes them.

source: An unauthenticated remote caller submits candidate email addresses to the tenant-admin challenge request route from the allowed tenant origin.
control: Live Chatwoot eligibility, exact-origin enforcement and a five-per-minute tenant/host+IP process-local limiter hold, but public success versus explicit TENANT_ADMIN_NOT_ELIGIBLE 403 semantics differ.
sink: The route reveals whether the candidate is an eligible Chatwoot administrator by response status/body and challenge/email progression.
impact: Tenant administrator membership can be enumerated for targeted phishing or credential attacks; the oracle does not itself grant access.
preconditions: Caller can issue same-origin requests to the public portal and has candidate email addresses; enumeration speed is constrained per IP/process.

evidence.result: The targeted integration test confirms an ineligible agent email receives the explicit 403 oracle and no code; the suite passed.
The per-process tenant/host+IP limiter reduces enumeration rate but does not equalize responses.
The existing finding requires indistinguishable public semantics and fully subsumes the source/control/sink/impact tuple.

source: An authenticated same-origin customer repeatedly uploads one avatar file of up to fifteen MiB for their own linked Chatwoot contact.
control: Exact-origin and customer-session checks, one-file/one-part limits, request and file-size caps, claimed MIME allowlist and upstream deadlines hold; no route-specific repetition limiter exists.
sink: Each accepted request buffers the file and performs one synchronous Chatwoot updateContactAvatar call for the current linked contact.
impact: Only proportional per-request backend/upstream work and self-profile mutation are proven; no cross-user/tenant effect, major amplification, durable corruption, cost escalation or service-wide exhaustion is established.
preconditions: Valid customer session, allowed origin, linked Chatwoot contact and repeated attacker bandwidth roughly equal to the bytes processed by the portal.

evidence.result: Targeted tests confirm one-file upload, current-linked-contact write and fifteen-MiB rejection behavior; all passed.
The route has no route-specific limiter, but the proven work remains bounded per request and self-scoped.
One part/file, exact origin, authentication and per-request byte bounds materially limit the claimed availability path.

source: An authenticated customer issues concurrent cold or recovery write/send operations for a thread whose Chatwoot conversation mapping must be bootstrapped.
control: A contact-scoped transaction advisory lock prevents duplicate conversation creation, but its handler remains inside the transaction and awaits external Chatwoot calls before release.
sink: The open database transaction and advisory lock are held across source-id resolution and createConversation network I/O while same-key waiters consume pool capacity.
impact: External latency can create database pool occupancy and a same-key convoy, degrading shared backend availability under concurrent cold/recovery traffic.
preconditions: Authorized writable thread with missing or stale conversation mapping, concurrent requests for the same target contact, and nontrivial Chatwoot latency; established threads bypass the path.

evidence.result: The transaction awaits a handler that performs external calls before the advisory transaction lock can release.
Targeted tests confirm scoped transaction locking and serialized concurrent bootstrap behavior; the suite passed.
The existing finding moves external work behind a durable short-transaction claim and fully subsumes the convoy tuple.

source: A public authentication attacker alternates attempts across backend replicas so each process counts only its local tenant/route/IP bucket.
control: Each process enforces a bounded five-per-minute tenant/host+IP map with Retry-After, but there is no shared atomic counter or account/code key across replicas.
sink: Multiple independent Fastify processes would each admit their own allowance to password, passwordless, reset, setup and tenant-admin verification routes.
impact: Horizontal scaling would multiply brute-force/request allowance across replicas; the represented reference production topology contains one backend process, so the bypass is conditional rather than currently instantiated.
preconditions: At least two backend processes behind traffic distribution and attacker ability to reach both; the supplied compose topology does not represent this state.

evidence.result: registerAuthRateLimit allocates one bounded Map per Fastify process with no external store.
Targeted integration tests confirm five requests are admitted and the sixth receives 429 within one process; the suite passed.
The repository's reference production topology represents one portal-backend service and no replica count.
The existing deferred finding requires shared counters before multi-instance deployment and fully subsumes the conditional tuple.

source: An authenticated thread participant repeatedly or concurrently submits a valid low-match search query against an accessible conversation with up to eight populated pages and distinct off-page reply targets.
control: Authentication, thread authorization, query length 2-80, eight scanned pages and twenty result cap hold, but there is no search request limit, total upstream-call budget, reply-target cache or bounded per-page lookup concurrency.
sink: Search scans up to eight history pages; every page Promise.all-resolves each unique missing reply target through Chatwoot, while list pages also perform cursor and older-history probes.
impact: The reproduced shape turns one portal request into eight page calls plus 160 reply-target calls at the client boundary, with additional lower-level list probes; concurrent repetition can consume backend outbound and Chatwoot request capacity disproportionately.
preconditions: Valid customer session, authorized conversation, eight pages of visible messages with distinct missing reply targets and a no-match query; an attacker can prepare reply history over time and then repeat searches.

evidence.result: A single search performed exactly eight history-page calls and 160 unique reply-target lookups in the bounded adversarial shape.
Each list call can perform the page request plus anchor and older-history probes; each reply lookup performs another history request.
Work is bounded to eight pages per request and requires suitable prepared or natural history, limiting severity below High.
No search-specific rate limit, cache, total-call budget or aggregate backpressure control appears on the exact route-to-client path.
